cards.explanation: The answer is Malta, friends. Acts 28:1 says that once they were safely ashore, they learned the island was called Malta. After a shipwreck, I bet a name on the map felt like a warm blanket.

The answer is that they kindled a fire and welcomed everyone. Acts 28:2 says the islanders "…kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold." A fire for a soaked crowd of strangers is about the best welcome I can think of. And they welcomed ALL of them, no picking and choosing.

The answer is viper, friends. Acts 28:3 says it was "…driven out by the heat…" and fastened itself to Paul's hand as he laid sticks on the fire. I would have hollered so loud the whole island heard me.

The answer is a murderer. In Acts 28:4 the islanders say to one another, "Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live." They saw the creature hanging from his hand and came to a big conclusion. I think we've all been quick to judge a situation we only half saw.

The answer is False. Acts 28:5 says Paul shook the creature off into the fire and "…suffered no ill effects." He just shook it off, like a man brushing crumbs off his apron. Then the islanders waited a long time and saw nothing unusual happen to him (Acts 28:6).

The answer is True. Acts 28:6 says that after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to Paul, the islanders changed their minds and said he was a god. They had a whole new opinion after watching a little longer. I'd have loved to hear that group chat.

The answer is that he welcomed them and hosted them for three days. Acts 28:7 says Publius "…welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days." Publius was the chief official of the island, and his estate stood nearby. Three days of hospitality is a real welcome.

The answer is that Paul prays and places his hands on him. Acts 28:8 says Paul went in to see the father of Publius, and "…after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man." Paul prayed first, and the man was healed. The father of Publius had been in bed with fever and dysentery.

The answer is the rest of the sick on the island, friends! Acts 28:9 says that after this had happened, "…the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well." It didn't stop with the father of Publius. I bet that was a lot of people to see.

The answer is True. Acts 28:10 says the islanders "…honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail." Think about that. They started with a fire on a cold beach and ended by sending the travelers off with what they needed. That's kindness from start to finish.
